description: Correction that changes when the innings ended
note: A dozens-of-deliveries, multi-over narrative (over 12.1 through 19.4) -- not practical as a literal fixture. TASK-0030's own change log flagged the same reduction: its InningsCorrectorTest.kt reproduces the exact STRUCTURAL property this example describes (ends_earlier_flags_orphaned_trailing_deliveries, no_longer_ends_flags_requires_continuation) via small purpose-built scenarios, at a scale that's actually reviewable, rather than transcribing this narrative verbatim.
blockedBy: requires the full multi-over event log this example describes; the underlying mechanism is already tested at a smaller scale by TASK-0030's InningsCorrectorTest.kt

narrative.preState: the recorded log shows over 19.4 as a wicket (the 10th, all out), innings recorded COMPLETE at that point; overs 19.5-19.6 never bowled.
narrative.correction: the scorer corrects over 12.1 (wrongly recorded as a wicket) to a leg-bye instead.
narrative.consequence: the batter dismissed at 12.1 is now not out and never left the crease; the batter who replaced them at 12.1 never batted; every event from 12.1 onward that referenced strike/bowler-of-record is now potentially inconsistent with the refolded reality.
narrative.handling: the engine does not attempt to auto-repair 19.4 or any event between 12.1 and 19.4 -- it surfaces every event whose recorded crease context now disagrees with the refolded derivation as a named, itemised reconciliation failure ("strike-context mismatch at over N.b"), blocking sign-off until the scorer works forward from 12.1 confirming or correcting each subsequent event's crease context explicitly (§19.2's principle: never silently reconciled on the scorer's behalf).
